max_log_file.description: Maximum number of audit log files to retain (after rotation). Must be ≥ 1.

num_logs.description: Number of log files kept after rotation. When exceeded, oldest logs are deleted.

log_group.description: Unix group ownership of the audit log file. Typically 'adm' or 'wheel'.

log_level.description: Verbosity level of audit logging: 0 (no logging), 1 (errors), 2 (recommended), 3 (verbose).

flush.description: Flush behavior for disk writes: 'sync' (safe, one write per event), 'data' (batched), 'incremental', or 'none' (high risk).

timeout.description: Seconds to wait before forcibly flushing buffers if flush is not 'sync'.

action_mail_acct.description: Account to email when disk space is low or audit daemon restarts.

admin_msg.default: Audit daemon unable to write to log
admin_msg.description: Message included in email alerts to the admin account.

log_file.description: Absolute path to the primary audit log file.

local.description: If enabled, log events locally. Disable only when using remote logging exclusively.

remote.description: If enabled, send audit logs to a remote server instead of (or in addition to) local logging.

remote_server.description: Hostname or IP address of the remote audit collector. Required if remote = true.

remote_port.description: Port number of the remote audit collector (usually 6080 for auditd protocol).

legacy.description: Enable legacy audit event format for compatibility with older tools.

use_ayat.description: If enabled, forward audit events to the systemd journal as well (not recommended for production).

extra_rules.description: List of custom audit rules to append to the configuration. Each entry defines a rule line and a comment.

line.description: The raw auditctl-style rule string (e.g., '-w /etc/passwd -p wa -k passwd_changes').

comment.description: A brief human-readable description of what this rule monitors.
